companies.description: Loft Orbital is a space infrastructure company operating under the banner "Space Made Simple" that integrates, launches, and operates low-Earth-orbit satellites so customers can fly physical payloads or deploy software "virtual missions" without building or operating their own spacecraft. Its Cockpit mission-control platform lets operators task payloads, monitor telemetry, and downlink data in real time through a secure web UI or an authenticated API, and a customer SDK provides frameworks, documentation, and satellite APIs (including Azure Orbital space-edge deploys) for onboard sensors and compute. The Cockpit API and developer docs are gated behind login at api.cockpit.loftorbital.com, so no public specification is available. Backed by Uncork Capital.

companies.name: Charter Space
companies.description: Charter Space is a London-based space technology company, founded in 2021, building software and financial infrastructure for the New Space economy. Its flagship product, Ubik, is a browser-native, model-based systems engineering and program management platform that unifies requirements management, project management, block diagrams, test procedures, and scheduling in a single collaborative environment, cutting manual systems-engineering admin for spacecraft programs. Ubik is in beta with organizations including teams at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and exposes native integrations (OneDrive, Google Drive, Jira, GitHub) plus an API for connecting specialized tooling. Charter has also expanded into space insurance, capturing manufacturing and test data at the source to feed an underwriting interface tied to the largest space-insurance carriers, and operates an insurance brokerage for New Space companies insuring satellites and spacecraft. Backed by Techstars and Capital Factory.

companies.name: Loft Dynamics
companies.description: Loft Dynamics is a Swiss aviation technology company (founded 2016, headquartered in Dübendorf, Switzerland with a North American office in Santa Monica) that builds virtual reality flight simulation training devices (FSTDs) for helicopters, fixed-wing aircraft, and eVTOLs. Its simulators combine full-scale replica cockpits, dynamic motion platforms, 360-degree VR visuals, and advanced pose tracking, and were the first VR aircraft simulators to earn EASA and FAA qualification. Products include VR simulators for the Airbus H145, Airbus H125, and Robinson R22 helicopters, with Boeing 737 and eVTOL platforms in development. Customers include Alaska Airlines, the FAA, Airbus Helicopters, the LAPD, and Marshall University. The company operates the LoftHUB customer platform but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

companies.name: Overstory
companies.description: Overstory provides AI-powered vegetation intelligence for electric utilities and grid operators. The platform fuses high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery with machine learning to detect vegetation encroachment, hazard trees, and wildfire risk along power line corridors, helping utilities prioritize trimming, optimize vegetation management spend, and improve grid reliability (SAIDI). Overstory was founded as 20tree.ai and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. As of this profile the company delivers its intelligence through a customer platform and services rather than a public developer API; no public API documentation, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

companies.name: Draxon
companies.description: Draxon is a Berlin-based company (founded 2025, backed by HV Capital and Point Nine) that provides IATA-certified virtual reality training for airport ground handling operations. The platform ships pre-configured Meta Quest VR headsets and an immersive training library covering ramp equipment such as belt loaders, tractors, pushback tugs, GPUs and towable stairs, plus safety procedures and hand signals for frontline ramp personnel. Its Trainer Hub delivers automated, IATA-compliant certification tracking with self-paced or instructor-led modules. Draxon operates as a B2B SaaS training provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: EyeLights
companies.description: EyeLights is a French deep-tech company building augmented reality head-up display (HUD) technology for riders and pilots. Its products project GPS navigation, speed, intercom, radar and call information into the rider's line of sight: EyeRide, a universal HUD accessory compatible with any motorcycle helmet; the GT-AIR 3 Smart, an integrated head-up display visor built into a SHOEI helmet; the APEX HUD glasses for general aviation; and Pulse Ultra, a universal Bluetooth intercom. The company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at eye-lights.com and runs customer support on Odoo. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; EyeLights publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so this record captures its consumer web, identity, and security posture rather than an API contract.

companies.name: Orbio
companies.description: Orbio Earth is a climate-tech company (founded 2021; Dover, Delaware, USA and Cologne, Germany) that turns open satellite data into industrial methane intelligence for the energy sector. Its platform detects, quantifies, and tracks methane emissions from oil-and-gas infrastructure globally at asset level with a roughly 5-day revisit rate, using multispectral imagery (Sentinel-2, Landsat 8/9, EMIT) and machine learning, plus Bayesian uncertainty estimation. Customers — oil-and-gas operators and private-equity firms — use it for super-emitter identification, historical trend and root-cause analysis, and compliance with emerging methane regulation. Platform access is offered via the web application or a sales-gated data API integration; there is no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK. Orbio also publishes the open-source Project Eucalyptus methane-detection pipelines on GitHub for research use.

companies.name: Kilsar
companies.description: Kilsar is an AI-powered maintenance training and operations platform for the aviation, defense, and industrial sectors. Its flagship product, Orion, turns static technical manuals and maintenance procedures into intelligent, guided workflows so technicians learn faster and perform complex tasks correctly. The platform provides AI-assisted search across operational and maintenance manuals, dynamic data storage and library management, custom workflow and procedure building, real-time task tracking and work-log monitoring, and predictive maintenance and troubleshooting guidance. Kilsar promises measurable outcomes including reduced downtime, faster mean-time-to-repair, and increased equipment uptime. Kilsar is a Techstars-backed company. As of this profile it publishes a marketing site and a Secureframe-hosted trust center but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: Comply365
companies.description: Comply365 is an enterprise SaaS provider of operational content, safety, and training management software for highly regulated, safety-critical industries including airlines, defense, rail, and MRO (maintenance, repair, and overhaul). Its AI-powered platform unifies three mission-critical products: ContentManager365 for authoring, managing, and distributing controlled operational documentation and manuals; SafetyManager365 for safety reporting, investigation, and root-cause analysis; and TrainingManager365 for workforce readiness and compliance training. Comply365 helps regulated operators shorten document change cycles, maintain regulatory compliance, and connect frontline teams to the current, approved content they need. The company is an Insight Partners portfolio company and is an ISO 27001 and ISO 9001 certified organization.

companies.name: Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings
companies.description: Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings is a global airfreight, charter, and aircraft leasing group headquartered in Purchase, New York and operating across more than 80 countries and 330+ airports. The holding company positions itself as the "Leader in Aviation Outsourcing" and runs three operating businesses: Atlas Air (ACMI, CMI, charter, and military/government cargo and passenger operations on Boeing 747-400F, 747-8F, 777F, 767, and 737-800BCF freighters), Polar Air Cargo (scheduled airport-to-airport cargo network, historically a joint venture with DHL), and Titan Aviation Leasing (commercial aircraft acquisition, leasing, and sale-leaseback services). Atlas is the largest operator of the Boeing 747 freighter, the Dreamlifter operator for Boeing, and one of the principal lift providers for Amazon Air's middle-mile network. In August 2022 a consortium led by Apollo Global Management with J.F. Lehman & Company and Hill City Capital agreed to take the company private in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately US$5.2 billion; the deal closed in March 2023, delisting the company (formerly Nasdaq: AAWW). As a freight carrier the group does not publish a public developer portal or open APIs — integrations with shippers, forwarders, and customers are delivered through private B2B channels (EDI, Cargo-IMP/XML messaging, airwaybill tracking on polaraircargo.com, and account-managed connectivity). A "Track Shipment" tool and a Special Loads request form (specialloads.atlasair.com) are the principal self-service surfaces; an internal-facing GitHub organization (Atlas-Air-Data-Platform) exists but publishes no public repos.

companies.name: CesiumAstro
companies.description: CesiumAstro designs, manufactures, and tests full-stack communication systems and satellites for space, air, and ground missions. The Austin, Texas company, founded in 2017, builds active phased array payloads (Vireo), software-defined radios (SDR-1001/2051/2104/3104), reconfigurable processing units, SATCOM terminals (Skylark), tactical ISR/PNT payloads (Nightingale), and the integrated Element LEO satellite platform. Its hardware enables inter-satellite links, high-speed downlinks, lunar communications, and 5G non-terrestrial networks. CesiumAstro publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; this profile tracks the company as an aerospace hardware provider in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: EnduroSat
companies.description: EnduroSat is a Sofia, Bulgaria-based satellite manufacturer and space service provider working to make space universally accessible by lowering the cost and complexity of accessing space data. The company builds CubeSat and SmallSat platforms (FRAME Max, FRAME L, FRAME S buses and 8U/12U/16U CubeSats), avionics and communication modules (X-Band SDR, S-Band and UHF transceivers, EPS power modules, solar panels, and antennas), and delivers end-to-end Space Service, SpaceOps, and SpaceDev offerings that take customers from idea to orbit in roughly six months. EnduroSat has deployed 100+ satellites with 3,500+ modules in operation, downlinked 500+ TB of data, and serves ~450 customers including NASA, ESA, and IBM Space. It maintains an open-source GitHub organization publishing Cubesat Space Protocol (CSP) implementations and NextGen ground-station and onboard API frameworks. Backed by Founders Fund and GV.

companies.name: Hula Earth
companies.description: Hula Earth is a Munich-based environmental technology company providing real-time biodiversity monitoring. It combines solar-powered, maintenance-free Hula BioT IoT sensors with AI-powered species detection, satellite-based Earth Observation, and the Hula Platform dashboard so organizations can monitor, manage, and report on biodiversity at landscape scale. Hula Earth serves renewables (solar and wind), agriculture, nature conservation, and urban development, turning environmental uncertainty into operational confidence and compliance-ready reporting.

companies.name: Isar Aerospace
companies.description: Isar Aerospace is a European space launch service provider founded in 2018 and headquartered in Ottobrunn near Munich, Germany. The company designs and manufactures Spectrum, a two-stage orbital small-lift launch vehicle capable of carrying up to 1,000 kg to low Earth orbit or up to 700 kg to Sun-synchronous orbit, using liquid oxygen and propane propulsion. Spectrum is fully developed and produced in-house with automated, scalable manufacturing including additive manufacturing and carbon-composite structures. Isar Aerospace offers dedicated, lead, and rideshare launch services for small and medium satellites and constellations. Backed by more than EUR 500 million in private capital from investors including Earlybird and HV Capital, the company employs over 400 people from nearly 50 nations and conducted the inaugural Spectrum test flight from Andoya Spaceport, Norway, on 30 March 2025.

companies.name: True Anomaly
companies.description: True Anomaly is a defense-technology company building spacecraft, software, and payloads for space superiority. Its products include Jackal, a multirole space-superiority platform positioned as a tactical fighter-interceptor for contested orbital environments, and Mosaic, an autonomy software platform that transforms commander intent into autonomous action. The company serves U.S. government and allied defense customers from facilities in Centennial and Colorado Springs, Colorado; Long Beach, California; and Washington, DC. True Anomaly publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; its only machine-readable public surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt vulnerability-disclosure contact.

companies.name: 1001 AI
companies.description: 1001 (also known as 1001 AI) is a deeptech artificial intelligence company founded in 2025 by Bilal Abu-Ghazaleh, a former director of generative AI operations at Scale AI, and headquartered between London and Dubai. The company builds sovereign AI operating systems for critical infrastructure — live operational models that help operators across aviation and airports, ports and logistics, energy and grids, construction, and manufacturing predict issues, automate and optimize decisions, and improve operational efficiency, while retaining full local ownership and governance of their AI systems. Focused primarily on the GCC and wider MENA region, 1001 raised a $9 million seed round in October 2025 led by CIV, General Catalyst, and Lux Capital, followed by a $30 million Series A in June 2026 led by Lux Capital with Sanabil Investments, 9Yards, and Hanabi joining and existing backers General Catalyst, CIV, and Stanford AI researcher Chris Ré increasing their commitments. As of this profile, 1001 publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK; this entry captures the company's public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Airspace Intelligence
companies.description: Air Space Intelligence (ASI) builds AI software for mission-critical, geospatial operations across aviation, defense, logistics, and energy. Its Prescience platform fuses data, models operational domains, runs predictive simulations, and optimizes complex operations in real time — spanning airline operations, air traffic management, global logistics, defense (space, air, land, sea), and energy grids. ASI holds an $875M FAA contract to help modernize the U.S. National Airspace System and works with partners including Alaska Airlines, National Grid, and the U.S. Air Force. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

companies.name: Boom
companies.description: Boom Supersonic is a Colorado-based aerospace company building Overture, a Mach 1.7 supersonic airliner designed to carry 64-80 passengers on transoceanic routes, powered by the company's Symphony engine and assembled at its Superfactory in Greensboro, North Carolina. Its XB-1 demonstrator flew supersonic in early 2025. Boom was surfaced as a portfolio company of SV Angel and added to the API Evangelist network. Boom publishes a corporate and investor-facing web presence (newsroom, careers, privacy, terms) but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, well-known discovery, or MCP surface, so no API artifacts are available to enrich; this profile captures its verifiable web and domain-security posture only.

companies.name: Boom Supersonic
companies.description: Boom Supersonic is a Denver-based aerospace company building supersonic commercial aircraft to make the world dramatically more accessible. Its flagship airliner, Overture, is designed to carry passengers at twice the speed of today's jets and has orders and pre-orders from United Airlines, American Airlines, and Japan Airlines. The company develops the Symphony medium-bypass turbofan engine purpose-built for supersonic flight, flew the XB-1 demonstrator past Mach 1, and is applying its propulsion technology to Superpower gas turbines for data-center energy. Boom is a deep-tech, hardware-first manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API surface; this profile tracks its identity and security posture in the API Evangelist network. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Electric Capital, and Homebrew.

companies.name: Canopy Aerospace & Defense
companies.description: Canopy Aerospace & Defense (Canopy A&D) is a vertically integrated advanced materials platform serving the aerospace, defense, space, maritime, and power-electronics industries. The company manufactures and delivers highly specialized materials with exceptional insulative, absorptive, and signal-reducing characteristics, including thermal protection systems (TPS), ultra-high-temperature ceramics, additive-manufactured ceramic components, multi-layer insulation and soft goods, and composite structures. Formed by Trive Capital through the combination of Canopy Aerospace, Hera Technologies, and MSM Industries, Canopy partners with OEMs from initial design and R&D through turnkey manufacturing and refurbishment of reusable platforms, operating facilities across the US, UK, and Netherlands. This is a physical materials manufacturer and publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its web and identity surface.

companies.name: Orbit Fab
companies.description: Orbit Fab is an in-space refueling company building "Gas Stations in Space" — the propellant supply infrastructure that lets satellites and spacecraft be refueled on orbit instead of being retired when their fuel runs out. Its offering centers on the RAFTI (Rapidly Attachable Fluid Transfer Interface) refueling port, the GRIP active grappling-and-resupply interface, a network of orbital Fuel Depots and Fuel Shuttles, and UMPIRE mission-planning software. Orbit Fab sells hydrazine and other propellant refueling services (including in GEO), and licenses RAFTI as a drop-in fill-and-drain valve replacement that the U.S. Space Force has recognized as a preferred refueling interface. The company is a hardware, aerospace, and space-logistics business; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched to record its identity and public-web surface.

companies.name: PierSight Space
companies.description: PierSight Space is an India-based space technology company building a constellation of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Automatic Identification System (AIS) satellites for persistent, all-weather maritime surveillance of the world's oceans. Founded by former ISRO engineer Gaurav Seth, PierSight delivers near-real-time ocean monitoring (targeting ~30-minute data latency and 100% ocean coverage) to detect illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing, monitor oil spills, protect Exclusive Economic Zones, support maritime insurance risk assessment, and improve shipping operations. The company has raised roughly $8M from investors including Alpha Wave Ventures, Elevation Capital, and Techstars. As of this enrichment pass PierSight sells data solutions to enterprise and government clients and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: Renoster Systems
companies.description: Renoster Systems is a carbon-credit ratings agency bringing deep transparency to the nature-based voluntary carbon markets. Using remote sensing, LiDAR, satellite data, and machine learning, Renoster independently rates forestry and other nature-based carbon offset projects, quantifying how much CO2 per credit a project has actually sequestered, and publishes public tools such as its Mercury project database and Renoster/Mercury rubric for researchers, reserve managers, policymakers, and corporate buyers. Renoster is a Techstars-backed startup. As of this profile the company does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface; this record captures its company identity and public web properties.

companies.name: Sarla Aviation
companies.description: Sarla Aviation is an Indian advanced air mobility company building electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft for urban transportation. Its flagship flying taxi, Shunya, uses a hybrid-electric propulsion system (seven electric units, dual battery packs, and a sustainable aviation fuel tank) to reach up to 250 km/h with a range up to 800 km and 150 km fully electric, in cabin configurations spanning 6-seat, 4-seat, cargo, and ambulance variants. Founded by former Lilium engineers Rakesh Gaonkar and Adrian Schmidt, the company is a portfolio company of Accel. The public website exposes no developer, API, or technical integration surface as of this enrichment pass; this profile captures corporate identity, legal, and domain-security signals only.

companies.name: Star Catcher
companies.description: Star Catcher is a space technology company building the first power grid in space. Its optical power beaming system, the Star Catcher Network, concentrates and transmits solar energy directly to satellites' existing solar arrays, delivering up to 10x more power without any hardware modifications. Founded in 2024 and backed by Initialized Capital, the company holds a world record for optical power beaming and is working to bring shared orbital power infrastructure to satellites supporting universal connectivity, advanced computing, and national security. Star Catcher raised $65 million in May 2026 and plans to bring its technology to orbit. Star Catcher operates physical space hardware and does not currently publish a public developer API.

companies.name: The Exploration Company
companies.description: The Exploration Company (TEC) is a European deep-tech space startup founded in July 2021 by Hélène Huby and a team of aerospace engineers from Airbus and ArianeGroup. Headquartered in Munich, Germany with sites in Bordeaux, Oberpfaffenhofen, Italy, France, Houston, and the MENA region, TEC develops Nyx, a family of modular, reusable, in-orbit refuelable spacecraft designed to carry cargo — and eventually humans — to low Earth orbit, lunar orbit, and the Moon, serving space stations and long-distance research missions. The company has raised a €40.5M Series A and a €150M Series B and is a certified B Corp. It exposes no public developer API; interfaces are provided to payload customers via a Payload User's Guide.

companies.name: World View
companies.description: World View (World View Enterprises) is a Tucson, Arizona-based stratospheric balloon company focused on remote sensing and persistent intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR). Its uncrewed high-altitude balloons carry EO/FMV, IR, SAR, and hyperspectral sensors for defense, government, and commercial missions. Acquired by Ondas Holdings in 2026, it now operates as part of the Ondas Sentinel multi-domain intelligence platform, with partnerships including Palantir and Sierra Nevada Corporation. World View publishes no public developer program or API.

companies.name: Worldview
companies.description: World View Enterprises (worldview.space) — incorporated in 2012 and headquartered in Tucson, Arizona — operates stratospheric balloons and high-altitude platforms for remote sensing, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), alongside a stratospheric space-tourism program. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, the company has completed more than 140 stratospheric flight operations for customers including NASA, NOAA, and the U.S. Department of Defense. World View was acquired by Ondas, Inc. in April 2026 and merged with DZYNE Technologies in July 2026 to form Ondas Sentinel. The company publishes no public developer API.

companies.name: Skylo
companies.description: Skylo Technologies is a satellite communications company based in Mountain View, California, operating a global Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) that lets standard smartphones and IoT cellular devices connect directly to satellites over 3GPP Release 17 direct-to-device (D2D) standards for SMS, sensor telemetry, and other low-bandwidth messaging. Founded in 2017 and backed by DCM, SoftBank, Intel Capital, Innovation Endeavors, BMW i Ventures, Samsung Catalyst, Next47, Seraphim Space, and NGP Capital, Skylo has commercial service across the US, Brazil, Australia, New Zealand, and Europe. Skylo does not publish a public REST/HTTP API; developer integration is device-level (certified modules such as Quectel, Murata, Blues Notecard and Particle) with detailed procedures gated behind a partner Knowledge Base. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company and its developer surface.

companies.name: Fetcherr
companies.description: Fetcherr is an Israel-based AI technology company (founded 2019, Netanya) building generative-AI decision systems for the aviation industry. Its core is the Large Market Model (LMM), a generative model trained on internal airline data plus external signals (competitor prices, demand, weather, events, economic indicators) to forecast markets and drive real-time business decisions. Fetcherr productizes the LMM as a Generative Pricing Engine (GPE) for dynamic airline pricing and as ALPHA, a cloud-based retailing and inventory-management platform that integrates with existing airline PSS and legacy infrastructure. Customers include Delta, Virgin Atlantic, WestJet, Azul, and Viva Aerobus. Fetcherr is an enterprise B2B vendor and does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or self-serve credentials; integration is delivered directly to airline customers. Added to the API Evangelist network as a battery-ventures portfolio company.

companies.name: Textron
companies.description: Textron Inc. is a $14.8 billion Fortune 500 multi-industry company employing 34,000 people worldwide. Textron operates through five business segments: Bell (military and commercial helicopters), Textron Aviation (Cessna, Beechcraft, Hawker aircraft), Industrial (Kautex fuel systems, Textron Specialized Vehicles including E-Z-GO and Jacobsen), Textron Systems (defense and autonomous systems), and Textron Financial. As of 2026, Textron does not offer publicly documented developer APIs or integration portals.

companies.name: Cognitive Space
companies.description: Cognitive Space is an aerospace software company delivering AI-powered automated satellite operations for constellation and fleet management. Its CNTIENT.Optimize platform automates mission planning, tasking, and multi-ground-station pass scheduling for satellite operators and government agencies, reporting large per-operator time savings, while CNTIENT.Earth delivers satellite Data-as-a-Service. The company integrates with customer systems via APIs and serves clients including Terran Orbital, the Space Development Agency, the Air Force Research Lab, and NOAA. Backed by Techstars.

companies.name: Morpheus Space
companies.description: Morpheus Space is an in-space mobility company building electric propulsion systems and mission-design software for the New Space economy. Founded in 2018 out of the Technical University of Dresden, its second-generation GO-2 system uses FEEP (Field Emission Electric Propulsion) technology to deliver continuous, chemical-free thrust for satellite constellation deployment, station keeping, collision avoidance, repositioning, and deorbiting. The company also offers Journey, a mission simulation and design platform that matches simulated requirements to available satellite subsystems. Morpheus Space markets ITAR-free solutions and is backed by investors including Techstars, Alpine Space Ventures, Airbus Ventures, Lavrock Ventures, and In-Q-Tel. The company publishes no public developer API; its only machine-facing surface is a platform-hosted (Wix) site MCP endpoint and an auto-generated llms.txt for agent access to public marketing content.

companies.name: Sylvera
companies.description: Sylvera is a London-headquartered carbon data and climate intelligence platform — often described as the "Moody's for the voluntary carbon market" — providing independent ratings, market data, and geospatial analytics that help corporate buyers, investors, project developers, governments, and standards bodies make informed decisions across carbon and commodities markets. Founded in 2020 by Allister Furey and Samuel Gill, Sylvera combines remote sensing, machine learning over satellite imagery and LiDAR-derived biomass data, and on-the-ground project assessment to produce letter-graded ratings (e.g., AA, A, B) for carbon credit projects across nature-based (REDD+, ARR, IFM), engineered removals, renewable energy, and cookstove methodologies. The platform's product surface spans Ratings, Market Intelligence (supply, demand, and pricing signals), an Article 6 & CORSIA Hub for compliance risk, a Market Gateway to roughly 400 million tonnes of project inventory, Earth Analytics and a Biomass Atlas for geospatial MRV, and Commodity Insights covering CORSIA, LCFS, CFR, and FuelEU Maritime mechanism eligibility and carbon intensity assessments. Sylvera distributes its data through a web platform, downloadable reports, and a gated Carbon Credit Analytics API (base URL https://api.sylvera.com/v1, JSON API style, API-key auth) used to syndicate ratings and pricing into ESG and sustainability reporting tools such as Workiva, Persefoni, and Watershed. Commercial packaging runs Freemium, Essentials, and Enterprise tiers, with Accelerated Ratings, Market Forecasts, and Geospatial add-ons all sold via contact-sales; there is no public OpenAPI specification, no published SDK, and no Sylvera GitHub organization — the API and full ratings catalog are available only to authenticated enterprise customers.

companies.name: Aptos Orbital
companies.description: Aptos Orbital (legal entity Cryptosat, Inc.) is a space technology company, founded in 2021 and backed by the Techstars Space Accelerator, that builds integrated hardware for satellites and spacecraft. Its flagship Aptos Terminal combines space-hardened, radiation-tolerant edge compute (with proprietary SEU/SEL protection), persistent global satellite communications, and cloud connectivity to platforms such as AWS and Azure into a single device. The company advertises 5.5+ years of proven orbital operation, 99% global data coverage, and TRL9 readiness for LEO applications, with development licenses, engineering models, and flight models offered to spacecraft builders. Aptos Orbital was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes hardware brochures and a "start developing" onboarding form but no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

companies.name: Zymbly
companies.description: Zymbly is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building a voice-first AI copilot for aircraft maintenance. Its AI agents automate the administrative half of a maintenance technician's day at airlines and MROs (maintenance, repair, and overhaul organizations): troubleshooting issues, looking up parts, retrieving technical documentation, and generating compliant paperwork so technicians can focus on the aircraft. Zymbly is a demo-led B2B product with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications at this time; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched from the company's public marketing site.

companies.name: Inmarsat
companies.description: Inmarsat is a British satellite communications operator founded in 1979, originally as the International Maritime Satellite Organization, providing voice, data, broadband, and IoT services over a global L-band, Ka-band, and multi-band fleet of geostationary satellites. In May 2023 Viasat completed its acquisition of Inmarsat, and the combined company now operates Inmarsat's GX (Global Xpress), BGAN, IsatData Pro (IDP), and Fleet Xpress services alongside Viasat's ViaSat-3 constellation as a unified multi-orbit network. Inmarsat serves four core markets — Maritime (NexusWave, Fleet Xpress, Fleet One, FleetBroadband, Inmarsat C/GMDSS), Aviation (SwiftBroadband, GX Aviation, Jet ConneX, SB-S safety services), Government (L-TAC, GX, BGAN M2M), and Enterprise/IoT (BGAN M2M, IsatData Pro, IsatM2M, NB-NTN). Inmarsat operates a developer program at developer.inmarsat.com with documented APIs for BGAN network management, GSPS voice, Global Xpress, IsatData Pro messaging, Fleet Edge assurance, and Fleet Edge hardware replacement; access to interactive Swagger documentation is gated behind developer registration and approval, though the IsatData Pro Messaging API has an open-source Apache-2.0 Node.js client published on GitHub. Inmarsat is also one of the participating operators in the GSMA NB-NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) standards work for satellite-extended cellular IoT, with Viasat-led proof-of-concept code for NIDD (Non-IP Data Delivery) published under the inmarsat-enterprise GitHub organization.

companies.name: Kepler Communications
companies.description: Kepler Communications operates a cloud-based infrastructure network in space, delivering real-time connectivity, on-orbit edge compute, and hosted payload services for satellite operators and space missions. Its offerings include the Kepler Network for space-based data relay and communications, Kepler Compute for on-orbit processing, and hosted payload services that reduce the cost and technical complexity of operating in orbit. Kepler is backed by Canaan Partners, Costanoa Ventures, and Techstars. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been identified; services are accessed through the Kepler customer portal and an Atlassian-hosted support service desk.

companies.name: Novo Space
companies.description: Novo Space develops high-performance, radiation-tolerant, modular electronics for the most ambitious space missions. Founded by Rodrigo Diez (CEO) and Facundo Jorge (CTO), the company builds SpaceVPX single-board computers, mass memory and GPU boards, tailored subsystems, and radiation-tolerant FPGA IP cores (SpaceWire, SpaceFibre, Ethernet/TCP-IP, CCSDS, NAND controllers, floating-point units) that let satellite and spacecraft builders reuse qualified hardware instead of re-engineering every mission. Customers and partners include Maxar, MIT, Thales Alenia Space, BAE Systems, Leonardo DRS, Mitsubishi, the US Air Force, Nvidia, Ansys, and Microchip. Novo Space is a space-computing hardware provider and does not publish a public web API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

companies.name: Air Space Intelligence
companies.description: Air Space Intelligence builds AI software for mission-critical aviation and defense operations. Its Prescience platform fuses live operational data, domain models, prediction, and optimization to give airlines, air-traffic managers, energy operators, and defense customers predictive situational awareness and decision support for complex, time-sensitive logistics. Product areas span airline operations, air traffic management, energy, global logistics, and defense (space, air mobility, land, and sea lift). The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass it publishes an enterprise marketing and hiring surface only — no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine discovery surface were found.

companies.name: AST SpaceMobile
companies.description: AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ, ASTS) is a United States satellite operator building the SpaceMobile Network, a space-based cellular broadband constellation of BlueBird satellites carrying the largest commercial phased-array antennas in low Earth orbit, designed to deliver 4G and 5G directly to standard, unmodified smartphones. It sits upstream of the retail telecom market as a wholesale coverage layer, not a consumer brand, not a CPaaS: signals from a handset are relayed by satellite to a small number of in-country ground gateways, which compensate for Doppler and delay and then hand the traffic into a mobile network operator's core, where the operator completes the call and bills the subscriber. Distribution runs entirely through partner carriers, with agreements covering nearly 60 mobile network operators serving over 3 billion subscribers, including AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, Rakuten, Bell, TELUS and stc, plus strategic investment from Google and American Tower. Its API posture is that of a satellite infrastructure company rather than a network-API publisher, honestly assessed as none: as of July 2026 AST SpaceMobile publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI, no SDKs and no public network-API surface. Probes of developer, developers, docs, api and opengateway subdomains and the corresponding site paths all fail to resolve or return 404, and no CAMARA, GSMA Open Gateway, TM Forum or 3GPP NEF exposure claim appears anywhere on ast-science.com or in its press releases. Any programmable access to SpaceMobile capacity reaches developers only indirectly, through the partner carrier that owns the subscriber relationship and the network APIs.

companies.name: Hermeus
companies.description: Hermeus is an American aerospace and defense company building rapidly reusable high-Mach and hypersonic aircraft for national-security missions in partnership with the U.S. Department of Defense. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, the company applies a hardware-rich, rapid design-build-test approach to move quickly from concept to flight. Its programs include Quarterhorse, a reusable high-speed flight-test aircraft; Darkhorse, a multi-mission reusable hypersonic uncrewed aerial system (UAS); and Chimera, a hybrid turbine-based combined-cycle engine that transitions from turbojet takeoff through supersonic flight into hypersonic acceleration. Hermeus is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile tracks the company's public web, security, and corporate properties in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Whisper Aero
companies.description: Whisper Aero is a Crossville, Tennessee based aerospace company developing ultra-quiet electric ducted-fan propulsion that converts electricity into thrust with roughly 20 percent more efficiency and 20 dB less noise than conventional systems, scaling from 5 to 500 pounds of thrust and 40 to 400 knots for aviation, defense, and commercial applications. Backed by Kindred Ventures, Lux Capital, and Menlo Ventures. The company is a hardware manufacturer and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Varda
companies.description: Varda Space Industries is a microgravity-enabled life sciences company that processes materials in orbit and returns them to Earth. Its in-house W-Series spacecraft are free-flying orbital production satellites with reentry capability, used for in-orbit pharmaceutical crystallization for biopharma partners and as a hypersonic reentry testbed for government flight testing. Backed by Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures, and Lux Capital, Varda publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

companies.name: Beyond Aero
companies.description: Beyond Aero is a French aerospace company building the world's first electric business aircraft powered by hydrogen propulsion. Its flagship aircraft, "One", is designed to fly more than 800 nautical miles with zero in-flight carbon emissions, targeting the light business-jet market. The company pairs rapid prototyping and iterative aircraft design with in-house engineering tools such as HADES (Hydrogen Aircraft Data Exploration Software). Backed by Initialized Capital, Beyond Aero is a frontier-tech hardware startup rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface at this time. This profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched with company identity and web/domain-security signals.

companies.name: Cowboy Space
companies.description: Cowboy Space Corporation builds space-based infrastructure for artificial-intelligence computing. Its flagship program, Stampede, is a constellation of solar-powered GPU data centers in Low Earth Orbit that integrate the rocket's upper stage with the satellite to form a megawatt-class data center with active thermal management and integrated compute. The company positions orbital compute as an alternative to terrestrial data centers, whose grid-connection lead times in major US markets can run five to seven years or more, arguing that Earth's energy grid cannot keep pace with AI demand. Cowboy Space is an early-stage aerospace and AI-infrastructure startup backed by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital; it currently publishes a corporate and careers presence with no public developer API.

companies.name: Cowboy Space Corporation
companies.description: Cowboy Space Corporation is a space infrastructure company building orbital data centers to address Earth's power constraints on artificial intelligence. Its Stampede satellite constellation places megawatt-class, GPU-equipped data centers in Low Earth Orbit powered by abundant solar energy, integrating the compute payload directly into the rocket's upper stage to maximize capacity and sidestep the multi-year terrestrial grid-connection delays that constrain traditional data centers. The company is an early-stage, venture-backed lead (backed by IVP); it currently publishes a corporate marketing site and careers portal but no developer portal, public API, or technical documentation.

companies.name: De-Ice
companies.description: De-Ice Technologies is a Somerville, Massachusetts deep-tech aviation startup building a chemical-free aircraft de-icing system that replaces conventional glycol spray with electrically heated strips applied to aircraft surfaces, removing snow and ice prior to takeoff. The technology eliminates weather-related departure delays, cuts glycol spraying costs, and reduces CO₂ emissions from idling fuel burn and chemical production. Named to Time's Best Inventions of 2024, De-Ice counts Air Canada as its launch customer and is backed by Techstars. This is a physical-hardware aviation company and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

companies.name: Scout
companies.description: Scout (Scout Space) is a Techstars- and venture-backed space technology company founded in 2019 that builds next-generation orbital sensing and autonomy for Space Domain Awareness (SDA). Its in-space products, first launched in 2021, let spacecraft see and understand objects around them through electro-optical and infrared sensors (the Owl long-range SDA sensor line), edge processing hardware, mission autonomy software developed with the U.S. Space Force, and mission-design analysis. Scout supplies cross-orbit intelligence and dynamic space operations to government and commercial operators and has been awarded multiple AFWERX SBIR and USSF TACFI contracts. Scout does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: TrustPoint
companies.description: TrustPoint, Inc. is a space technology company building a fully commercial, next-generation global navigation satellite system (GNSS) — a C-band LEO microsatellite constellation delivering secure positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) independent of GPS, with improved accuracy, faster time to first fix, and anti-jamming / anti-spoofing capabilities for automotive, aviation, critical infrastructure, and national security applications. Headquartered in Northern Virginia with an office in Mountain View, California, and backed by DCVC, TrustPoint does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

companies.name: Zipline
companies.description: Zipline is a South San Francisco–headquartered autonomous logistics company operating the world's largest commercial drone delivery network, with more than two million customer deliveries flown across the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, and Japan. Zipline designs, builds, and operates two end-to-end aircraft platforms: Platform 1 (P1, "Sparrow"), a long-range fixed-wing aircraft that launches from a catapult, parachutes payloads from altitude, and is used primarily for national-scale healthcare logistics — delivering blood products, vaccines, medicines, and lab samples to hospitals and clinics — and Platform 2 (P2), a short-range hybrid VTOL aircraft with an autonomous tethered "droid" delivery vehicle that lowers packages from a hovering aircraft directly to a designated point on the ground, enabling precision quick-commerce delivery from restaurants, retailers, pharmacies, and hospitals. Zipline's customer roster includes Walmart, OhioHealth, Michigan Medicine, Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic Florida, MultiCare, Sweetgreen, GNC, Jet's Pizza, the governments of Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, and Kenya, and Japan's Toyota Tsusho, with the P2 platform actively scaling across the Dallas–Fort Worth Metroplex, Pea Ridge (AR), and expanding into Houston and Phoenix in 2026. The company also operates one of the largest civil autonomous aviation stacks in the world — proprietary detect-and-avoid, route planning, weather, fleet operations, and flight-control software — and in 2025 received the first-ever FAA Part 135 BVLOS (beyond-visual-line-of-sight) operational approval permitting drone package delivery without visual observers. Zipline is a privately held company; its revenue model is drone-as-a-service contracts with healthcare systems, retailers, restaurant brands, and governments. There is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, GitHub organization, status page, changelog, or self-service developer portal — integrations with customer systems (order management, EHR, WMS, dispatch) are delivered as managed enterprise integrations rather than as a public programmable API.

companies.name: GE Aerospace
companies.description: A leading manufacturer of jet engines and aviation systems for commercial and military aircraft. Spun off from General Electric to focus exclusively on aerospace propulsion and services, GE Aerospace also offers software-as-a-service tooling, engine health monitoring (Collaborative Insight), TRUEngine certification, and OnPoint maintenance and support services.

companies.name: Esper Satellite Imagery
companies.description: Esper Satellite Imagery is an Australian space-technology company building an 18-satellite hyperspectral Earth-observation constellation (the Over The Rainbow / OTR program) to deliver global chemical-composition data of the planet's surface from orbit. Its Esperesso hyperspectral imagers capture more than 100 contiguous spectral bands spanning roughly 400 to 1000 nm, which Esper turns into mineralisation maps that identify lithium, rare earths, gold, nickel, cobalt and alteration zones for critical-mineral exploration — faster, cheaper and greener than traditional ground surveys. Founded in 2021 in Melbourne, Victoria by Iqbal and Joey Lorenczak, Esper sells custom area-of-interest mineral maps and a pre-built Northern Territory mineral map. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, security and code-repository surface.

companies.name: Firefly Aerospace
companies.description: Firefly Aerospace is an end-to-end space transportation company building the Alpha small-lift rocket, the Eclipse (formerly MLV) medium-lift vehicle, the Blue Ghost lunar lander, and the Elytra orbital vehicle (with the Ocula lunar imaging service). Firefly sells launch, lunar delivery, and on-orbit services through sales and payload-user-guide channels; it does not publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Brumby
companies.description: Brumby (formerly GrazeMate) is a Y Combinator-backed (W2026) precision-grazing company based in Sydney, Australia, building an autonomous drone toolkit for cattle ranchers. Brumby drones plan routes and move herds with gentle, AI-guided pressure, fly scheduled monitoring missions that locate and count every animal, measure standing dry-matter pasture biomass from the air, and inspect water troughs, tanks and fences on every flight — all managed from a single phone app that works online or in a local base-station mode without connectivity. The company is running pilot programs and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile is a company lead maintained in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Impulse Space
companies.description: Impulse Space is an American aerospace company founded in 2021 by Tom Mueller, building in-space transportation and mobility infrastructure. The company designs and operates orbital transfer vehicles (OTVs) that host, maneuver, and deliver payloads across and between orbits for commercial, civil, and government customers. Its product line includes Mira, an agile spacecraft for precise payload hosting and deployment across any orbit; Helios, a high-energy kick stage capable of moving up to 4,000 kg of payload from Low Earth Orbit to Geostationary Orbit in under 24 hours; and a GEO Rideshare program offering economical access to geostationary orbit. Impulse Space is a hardware and launch-services company rather than a software API provider, and does not publish a public developer portal, API, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and Founders Fund and enriched from the company's public website.

companies.name: Involve Space
companies.description: Involve Space is an Italian stratospheric aerospace company building real-time Earth intelligence. It operates autonomous high-altitude balloon platforms (Stratostats) that loiter around 20 kilometers for hours, days, or weeks to deliver continuous, high-resolution Earth observation, bridging the gap between satellites, drones, and ground sensors. Its Neurostar AI flight software autonomously controls individual balloons and networks of them (LoonHive), while the CLEAR GeoAI platform turns captured imagery into geospatial insights for disaster response, infrastructure and environmental monitoring, security, and in-orbit-demonstration / payload validation. A certified B Corporation headquartered in Italy with U.S. operations at the Houston Spaceport, Involve Space is backed by Earlybird Venture Capital, CDP Venture Capital, and an EIC Accelerator grant.

companies.name: IONA
companies.description: IONA (IONA Drones) is a UK-based autonomous drone delivery company building the full technology stack for logistics operators. Its tilt-rotor Sonnet aircraft performs VTOL from compact sites and carries up to 20 parcels up to 200 km per autonomous flight. IONA pairs the aircraft with an onboard autonomy operating system, GPS/LiDAR sensor-fusion precision landing, a SORA-aligned BVLOS compliance engine, an operations centre for real-time fleet monitoring and analytics, and a digital twin for simulation and predictive maintenance. The platform integrates with existing TMS/WMS logistics systems and targets healthcare, rural/remote, express e-commerce, industrial, and maritime delivery. Backed by Techstars.

companies.name: Savion Aerospace
companies.description: Savion Aerospace (FlySavion) is an aerospace company developing sustainable, zero-emissions aviation technology. Its flagship SavionJet is an autonomous blended-wing-body (ABWB) aircraft with a standup cabin and satellite-based piloting via proprietary autonomous flight software, and the company offers Zero-Emissions Flight Credits (ZFCs) as a subscription for organizations seeking carbon-free air travel beyond offsetting. Savion demonstrated a cryogenic LNG-fueled flight in 2019 and is a 500 Global (500 Startups) and Alchemist Accelerator portfolio company. The company operates as an aviation hardware and services business and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Stoke Space
companies.description: Stoke Space Technologies is an American space launch company based in Kent, Washington, founded in 2020 by a team of former Blue Origin and SpaceX engineers, led by co-founders Andy Lapsa and Tom Feldman (both ex-Blue Origin). The company is developing Nova, a medium-lift, 100% fully reusable rocket aimed at dramatically lowering the cost of access to orbit, along with its Zenith full-flow staged-combustion first-stage engine, the Andromeda second-stage engine, and a reusable metallic reentry heat shield. Stoke operates a 168,000 sq ft assembly facility and headquarters in Kent and a rocket test site near Moses Lake, Washington. Backed by Spark Capital and others, the company extended its Series D financing to $860 million in 2026. Stoke Space is a physical aerospace/hardware manufacturer and launch provider; it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

companies.name: Windward
companies.description: Windward is a Maritime AI company headquartered in London and Washington D.C. delivering mission-grade, multi-source maritime intelligence for defense agencies, law enforcement, customs, energy and commodity traders, marine insurers, shippers, and financial institutions. Founded by CEO Ami Daniel, Windward fuses AIS data, remote sensing (EO, SAR, RF GEOINT), proprietary behavioral analytics, and generative AI into a single Maritime AI platform covering vessel screening, ownership and entity resolution, sanctions exposure, deceptive shipping detection, ship-to-ship transfer analysis, IUU fishing detection, smuggling detection, container tracking, and maritime infrastructure protection. Windward exposes its intelligence through the API Insights Lab, a unified GraphQL API at developer.windward.ai providing programmatic access to vessel risk scores, Organization Defined Risk (ODR), ultimate beneficial ownership, early detection signals, tracked shipments, carriers, and detention & demurrage data, along with webhooks and workflow automation. The company has no public REST/OpenAPI surface, no public SDKs, and no public GitHub org — its API is GraphQL-only with managed onboarding and expert-led implementation support.

companies.name: Muon Space
companies.description: Muon Space is a Mountain View, California-based end-to-end space systems company that designs, builds, and operates mission-optimized satellite constellations to deliver Earth Intelligence and enable real-time compute and decision-making in space. Founded in 2021 by veterans of Skybox, NASA, and SpaceX, the company's core product is Muon Halo, an integrated technology stack composed of MuSim (constellation simulation and digital twin), MuOS (IP-based software-defined network middleware connecting space, ground, and cloud), MuCore (software-configurable instrument core), Condor (modular Condor-M and Condor-XL spacecraft platforms), and MuDash (cloud-based tasking, scheduling, and operations dashboard). Muon Space's flagship public mission is FireSat, a purpose-built wildfire detection and monitoring constellation developed with the Earth Fire Alliance, Google Research, and the Gordon & Betty Moore Foundation; FireSat carries a high-dynamic-range multispectral IR instrument capable of detecting 5x5 meter fires across a 1,500 km swath with a 50 m nadir ground sample distance, with revisit times targeted to twenty minutes once the full constellation is operational. The Protoflight satellite produced its first-light imagery in June 2025, with the first block of three additional satellites launching in 2026 and full operational capacity targeted for 2030. Other Muon Space missions support the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Space Force for next-generation weather monitoring, Hydrosat for thermal geospatial intelligence in climate and agriculture, and global security applications including missile-defense architecture. Muon Space's revenue model is mission contracting, spacecraft and constellation delivery, and hosted data services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of the Halo platform or FireSat data feed.

companies.name: Birdstop
companies.description: Birdstop is an American autonomous-drone and remote-sensing company that lets organizations monitor and inspect field assets at scale without personnel onsite. Its Fealty system is an all-weather, always-on drone that launches in under three seconds, flies for up to 45 minutes, cruises at 45 mph, and patrols 24/7 across public safety, utilities, transportation, construction, and data-center sites. Birdstop pairs networked UAVs and ground stations with computer vision and a patented optical/acoustic detect-and-avoid system to enable safe beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight under some of the FAA's most advanced approvals, delivering Observation-on-Demand intel over the internet. The company is FAA-authorized, SOC 2 certified, and NDAA compliant, and builds its drones in Detroit. Backed by Techstars, Birdstop currently exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Northwood Space
companies.description: Northwood Space is an El Segundo, California ground-infrastructure company for the space industry, founded in 2022 by Bridgit Mendler (CEO), Griffin Cleverly (CTO), and Shaurya Luthra. It designs and delivers rapidly deployable satellite ground stations built on electronically steerable phased-array antennas that track many satellites at once with no moving parts, paired with software ("Portal") that orchestrates every contact, automates scheduling, and moves data from spacecraft to customer. Northwood aims to turn ground infrastructure into cloud-like, on-demand global capacity for defense and commercial operators. The company's software stack is described as developer-oriented with modern APIs and integration hooks, but it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Founders Fund, Washington Harbour Partners, and Alpine Space Ventures; raised a $100M Series B and won a $50M Space Force contract in early 2026.

companies.name: B/E Aerospace
companies.description: B/E Aerospace was a manufacturer of aircraft cabin interior products and a provider of aerospace services for commercial aircraft and business jets. The company was acquired by Rockwell Collins in 2017 and subsequently merged into Collins Aerospace (a Raytheon Technologies subsidiary) in 2020. B/E Aerospace products included seating, food and beverage preparation equipment, lighting systems, and oxygen systems for commercial and business aviation.

companies.name: Ampaire
companies.description: Ampaire is a Long Beach, California electric aviation company that develops hybrid-electric propulsion systems for aircraft. Its AmpDrive powertrain retrofits and powers regional aircraft, and the company reports more than 30,000 flight miles with a stated goal of cutting fuel consumption, maintenance costs, and noise. Ampaire is backed by Techstars and has worked with partners including NASA and ARPA-E. The company currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record awaiting any future developer program.

companies.name: GATE Space
companies.description: GATE Space is an Austrian aerospace company redefining in-space mobility with high-thrust chemical propulsion systems for satellites, capsules, and landing vehicles. A TU Wien spinout founded in 2022 and backed by Techstars, the company builds the GATE Jetpack — a plug-and-play, refuelable propulsion module running on green propellants that lets satellites perform rapid orbit and attitude maneuvers with no integration effort. Its patented engines have been validated across 8,000+ hot-fire tests in atmospheric and vacuum conditions, manufactured in a European facility with a 98% local supply chain. GATE Space raised €6.3M via the EIC Accelerator and its propulsion system will fly on BeaconSat, Austria's first military satellite. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer/API surface; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record.

companies.name: Kela Technologies
companies.description: Kela Technologies (kela.io) is a defense technology company founded by veterans of elite Israeli intelligence units, providing a secure, open platform that enables rapid and seamless integration of commercial and military systems in service of Western defense. The company emerged from stealth in 2025 after raising $39M from Sequoia Capital, Lux Capital, and In-Q-Tel (the CIA's venture arm). Kela is building "Sovereign Sky," a low-Earth-orbit satellite constellation for resilient communication and navigation independent of foreign infrastructure, and acquired cloud-management company Pelanor. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a single-page marketing site with a privacy policy but no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable interface.

companies.name: Rolls-Royce
companies.description: Rolls-Royce plc is a British multinational aerospace and defense company manufacturing aero engines (Trent series), defense propulsion, and power systems. Rolls-Royce does not publish a public developer API. The company operates supplier portals at suppliers.rolls-royce.com and maintains a small GitHub presence with the qc-cfd open-source repository covering quantum computing for computational fluid dynamics research.

companies.name: Astro Mechanica
companies.description: Astro Mechanica is a San Francisco aerospace company, founded in 2021 by Ian Brooke, reinventing supersonic flight for a new jet age. Its flagship Duality electric combined-cycle engine is engineered to stay efficient from takeoff through Mach 3+ by reconfiguring between turbofan, turbojet, and ramjet modes using a hybrid turboelectric architecture. The company designs engines, airframes, and flight systems in-house, has been selected to develop an engine for the U.S. Air Force Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program, and is backed by a16z, Lowercarbon Capital, and Y Combinator. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company. As an aerospace hardware manufacturer, Astro Mechanica publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web and identity surface only.

companies.name: AstroForge
companies.description: AstroForge is a commercial space startup founded in 2022 and based in Huntington Beach, California, focused on asteroid mining and the in-space extraction and refining of platinum group metals and other critical minerals. Backed by Initialized Capital and a Y Combinator alum, the company designs low-cost, autonomous, replicable interplanetary spacecraft to prospect and mine near-Earth asteroids, with its DeepSpace-2 mission targeting the first commercial rendezvous with a body outside Earth's gravity well. AstroForge does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a frontier-tech lead and will be enriched further if and when a developer program appears.

companies.name: Catalyx Space
companies.description: Catalyx Space Inc. is a San Francisco based space infrastructure company building an integrated platform for deploying payloads to low Earth orbit and returning them safely to the ground. The company develops autonomous orbital labs and reusable reentry vehicles (ReX) that use origami-inspired hypersonic decelerator technology to deliver heavy-mass downmass from orbit to ocean recovery zones, positioning itself as the fastest and most affordable way to deploy experiments and manufacture in orbit. Catalyx handles end-to-end space operations including spacecraft development, payload integration, launch logistics, mission control, and recovery. Surfaced as a Techstars (and Outlander) portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the company currently publishes a marketing and careers presence but no public developer API surface.

companies.name: Heart Aerospace
companies.description: Heart Aerospace is a hybrid-electric aircraft manufacturer founded in 2019 and headquartered in Torrance / Los Angeles, California, working to decarbonize and lower the cost of regional air travel. The company is developing the X1, a full-scale hybrid-electric technology demonstrator, and the ES-30, a 30-seat regional production aircraft, backed by strategic airline partners including United Airlines and Air Canada and investors such as Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, EQT Ventures, and Y Combinator. Heart Aerospace publishes no public developer or API surface; this profile tracks the company as an API Evangelist network entry in the sustainable-transport sector.

companies.name: Orbital Arc
companies.description: Orbital Arc is a Houston-based deep-tech spacecraft propulsion startup founded in 2023 by Jonathan Huffman, building Gas-Phase Field Effect Electric Propulsion (Gas FEEP) thrusters and the RIOT Drive (Relativistic Ion Thrust Drive) for satellites and in-space transportation. Its ultra-lightweight electric thrusters use solid naphthalene fuel that sublimates at room temperature instead of noble gases, targeting high specific impulse for satellite constellations. Backed by Techstars and Capital Factory, the company completed a sub-scale physics demonstration at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (TRL 3). This is a hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer surface as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Reflect Orbital
companies.description: Reflect Orbital is a space-technology company developing satellite-based infrastructure to redirect natural sunlight to precise locations on Earth. It offers a Lighting service (adjustable illumination from moonlight to full-daylight intensity, controllable via app or website with no ground infrastructure) and an Energy service (augmenting solar-farm output by directing concentrated sunlight onto photovoltaic arrays). The company plans to expand its constellation from 2 satellites in 2026 toward 50,000+ by 2035. Reflect Orbital is backed by Lux Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced company profile. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, pricing, or sign-up surface.

companies.name: Solestial
companies.description: Solestial is a space solar energy company developing space-stable silicon photovoltaics — radiation-hardened, ultrathin flexible silicon heterojunction solar cells and modules for spacecraft. Its products are the only solar products on the market that self-cure radiation damage at operating temperatures, offering competitive performance at lower cost than III-V multijunction solar. Solestial has flight heritage across multiple spacecraft and works with customers including NASA, Boeing, and the U.S. Space Force. This is a hardware and manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

companies.name: The Exploration Company
companies.description: The Exploration Company GmbH is a European space transportation startup building reusable space vehicles "for humanity." Its flagship program, Nyx, is a reusable capsule designed to carry cargo and, eventually, crew between Earth and low Earth orbit destinations such as commercial space stations, featuring orbital propulsion, autonomous docking, and re-entry recovery. The company is also developing Storm, a high-thrust reusable rocket engine (up to 180 tons of thrust) built through European partnerships toward a globally competitive launcher. Backed by Balderton Capital and a certified B Corp, it markets itself as one of the fastest-growing space startups in the world. The company operates a marketing and careers web presence but publishes no public developer program, API, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time. Surfaced as a Balderton Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network with verified identity and domain-security signals.

companies.name: VXB Aerospace
companies.description: VXB Aerospace is an Australian space technology company founded in 2022 by Alexander Ryan, developing generative design software and Hall-effect plasma propulsion for the satellite market. Its platform automates the design, manufacturability analysis, multi-physics modeling and validation of complex aerospace hardware such as propulsion systems, antennas and satellite layouts, while its ZEPHYR-35 Hall-effect thruster (Argon/Krypton/Xenon) provides in-orbit mobility, refueling, servicing and de-orbiting. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

companies.name: Pachama
companies.description: Pachama is a San Francisco–based climate technology company founded in 2018 that built a satellite- and machine-learning-powered platform for monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of nature-based carbon projects — including forest conservation, reforestation, afforestation, and improved forest management. Pachama combined satellite imagery, LiDAR, remote sensing, and deep-learning models to measure aboveground biomass, detect deforestation, and track project performance against verified baselines, surfacing that intelligence through an online marketplace where corporate buyers (including Microsoft, Shopify, Salesforce, Flexport.org, Mercado Libre, Boom Supersonic, and Nespresso) could discover and purchase high-integrity carbon credits. In November 2025, Pachama was acquired by Carbon Direct, and its proprietary digital MRV platform and forest-carbon science team were folded into Carbon Direct's science-backed carbon management offering; pachama.com now redirects to carbon-direct.com. Throughout its life as an independent company Pachama operated a buyer marketplace and discussed plans for a partner API to embed project selection and retirement data into third-party products, but never shipped a public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open OpenAPI specification — its GitHub organization contains only forks and archived internal tooling.

companies.name: Wing
companies.description: Wing is Alphabet's drone delivery subsidiary, spun out of Google X in 2018, with operating headquarters in Palo Alto, California and significant operations in Australia, Finland, Ireland, and the United States. Wing designs, builds, and operates a fleet of small fixed-wing electric VTOL aircraft that autonomously pick up and deliver packages to customers' homes, and it operates an unmanned traffic management (UTM) stack used by drone pilots and aviation authorities. Wing was the first company to receive an FAA Part 135 Air Carrier Certificate for drone delivery (2019) and is an approved LAANC USS in the United States and an approved drone airspace authorization provider for CASA in Australia. Wing's commercial surface is split across two main platforms — the Wing Delivery Platform, a partner-only API and UI suite that lets retailers, restaurants, and logistics providers embed drone delivery into their own order flows (Walmart, DoorDash, Papa Johns, and others), and OpenSky, a consumer drone airspace authorization app and partner API. Wing also co-founded the InterUSS Platform open-source UTM project, now hosted by the Linux Foundation. Wing's revenue comes from per-delivery fees charged to merchant partners and from drone-as-a-service operations rather than from public developer APIs; the Delivery Platform API and OpenSky API are not openly published and there is no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at the time of profiling.

companies.name: BioOrbit
companies.description: BioOrbit is a London-based in-space manufacturing company, founded in 2023, that uses microgravity to crystallise protein-based biologic drugs at scale. Its autonomous BOX hardware — a compact, microwave-sized manufacturing unit designed to operate in low-Earth orbit — grows highly ordered crystalline forms of therapeutic proteins that reduce viscosity, enabling treatments normally given intravenously (including cancer therapies) to be reformulated as subcutaneous, self-injectable products. Co-founded by Dr Katie King and Dr Leonor Teles, BioOrbit raised the world's largest seed round for in-space manufacturing (~£9.8M / $13.2M) co-led by LocalGlobe and Breega with Seedcamp, Auxxo, Type One, 7percent and angels, and is supported by the UK Space Agency, ESA BIC and ESA BSGN. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Seedcamp portfolio company; it publishes no public API or developer surface.

companies.name: Arctus Aerospace
companies.description: Arctus Aerospace is a Bengaluru, India based deep-tech startup building high-altitude, long-endurance autonomous unmanned aircraft (MALE/HALE UAVs) for real-time Earth observation and geospatial intelligence. Its platforms are designed to operate near 45,000 feet for over 24 hours while carrying payloads up to 250 kg, delivering centimeter-level multispectral imagery as a "zero-infrastructure" alternative to satellites. The company positions itself as a data-as-a-service provider, selling subscription-based aerial coverage for energy, infrastructure, climate, defense, and agriculture use cases. Founded in 2024 by Shreepoorna S. Rao, Arctus raised a $2.6M pre-seed round led by Version One Ventures (with South Park Commons, gradCapital, and angels). As of this writing the company is pre-product from an API standpoint and publishes no public developer surface, API, or documentation; this profile was surfaced as a Version One Ventures portfolio lead.

companies.name: Kairos Aerospace
companies.description: Kairos Aerospace is a methane-detection company founded in 2014 in Sunnyvale, California that provides cost-effective, high-frequency aerial methane detection for the oil and gas industry. Its patented LeakSurveyor spectrometer is flown over upstream and midstream infrastructure to image methane plumes, and proprietary software turns those flights into actionable emissions data so operators can find, prioritize, and fix leaks. The company rebranded as Insight M in March 2024 and was subsequently acquired by Zeitview. Kairos Aerospace was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile is an identity record rather than an API catalog entry.

companies.name: Axionorbital Space
companies.description: AxionOrbital Space is a San Francisco Bay Area startup (Y Combinator Winter 2026) building foundation models for continuous Earth observation through clouds and darkness. Its flagship model, ORION, converts Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into high-resolution, photorealistic optical imagery in real time using deterministic one-step diffusion, overcoming the limitation that traditional optical satellites are unusable roughly 70% of the time due to weather and night cycles. The technology targets 24/7 situational awareness for defense and intelligence, commodities and financial analytics, disaster response, agriculture, and climate monitoring. Founded in 2025 by Dhenenjay Yadav (CEO, former ISRO ML engineer) and Atharva Peshkar (CTO, PhD, CU Boulder / Harvard VCG). At the time of profiling the company is pre-product with no public API, developer portal, or specifications published; this record captures its identity for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Kuva Space
companies.description: Kuva Space is a Finnish space-data company headquartered in Espoo that operates a fleet of hyperspectral Earth observation microsatellites and delivers AI-driven planetary intelligence through its Kuva Sense platform. Founded in 2016 (originally as Reaktor Space Lab) by Tuomas Tikka and Janne Kuhno in collaboration with Reaktor, the company designs, builds, and operates its own 6U CubeSat-class spacecraft carrying a patented in-orbit tunable Fabry-Perot 2D snapshot hyperspectral imager. Its operational Hyperfield-1A (launched August 2024 on SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg) and Hyperfield-1B (launched June 2025) cover the 475–950 nm VNIR range with up to 160 tunable spectral bands at 25 m spatial resolution and a 50 km swath from a 500 km polar sun-synchronous orbit. The larger 70 kg Hyperfield-2 microsatellite, scheduled for H2 2026, expands coverage to 450–1,650 nm at 15 m resolution with an additional 3.6 m GSD RGB camera. By 2030 Kuva Space plans to grow the constellation to roughly 100 satellites to enable sub-daily revisit anywhere on Earth. Onboard AI handles cloud filtering, spectral band alignment, and compression so that downlinked products feed directly into Kuva Sense, where automated analytics generate insights-as-a-service for agriculture (crop identification, yield forecasting, harvest timing), aquaculture (water quality, algal bloom detection, biomass), environment and carbon (sequestration monitoring, deforestation, pollution tracking), and safety and security (vessel detection and tracking, illegal activity warning, rapid change detection). Kuva Space is part of the European Space Agency InCubed-co-funded HYPERFIELD program, was awarded a €1.8M ESA Civil Security from Space contract within the SMART-CONNECT consortium to demonstrate rapid hyperspectral insights for crisis response, and in 2026 signed a Letter of Intent with SSC Space to strengthen Nordic space capabilities. The commercial model is subscription-based insights-as-a-service rather than pay-per-pixel imagery sales, with current access offered through the Kuva Sense Early Adopter Program; the company markets "robust APIs and customizable data formats" for system integration but does not currently publish open public API reference documentation, an OpenAPI specification, or a self-service developer portal. The only public engineering surface is the open-source kuva-data-processing Python toolkit (kuva-metadata, kuva-reader, kuva-geometry) on GitHub and PyPI, which reads Kuva GeoTIFF-based L0/L1AB/L1C/L2A data products and their metadata sidecars.

companies.name: Orbital Insight
companies.description: Orbital Insight was a Palo Alto, California geospatial analytics company founded in 2013 by James Crawford (formerly Bell Labs, Google Books, and NASA's Mars rover program).
